parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, no documented border friction for foreign passports, no facility-ban or marker-disclosure rule reaching visitors — so no tier-1 universal exposure. But enforcement lags the statute: a 2024 bank refusal on document/appearance mismatch (Equality Council confirmed, only recommended measures), serious unanswered hate speech, freedom of assembly arbitrarily restricted, and acceptance extremely low (79% would not accept LGBT neighbours). Police protected recent Pride but earlier failed to protect marchers and declined to investigate an arson against an LGBT lawyer. A 2025 prison case shows birth-sex placement, isolation and staff humiliation in custody. Paper protections exist but are only patchily operative; unmapped areas (immigration detention, rural officers) keep uncertainty.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border friction for trans visitors; foreign passports and markers are not shown to be challenged. No X-marker recognition data, no scanner/pat-down practice, no immigration-detention conditions documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry is a documentation encounter the visitor cannot avoid; the record is silent on it rather than reassuring, though nothing suggests referral for appearance mismatch.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented 2025 case: trans man held in the penitentiary system by birth sex, three years effectively alone in rat-infested cells, protection-unit transfer refused, forced strip searches, female name at roll-call; administration denies violations. Police refused to investigate a 2019 arson on an LGBT lawyer's car.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Authorities state staff training and stricter anti-harassment penalties are being prepared; ombudsman and local LGBT group notified of the case.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Custody placement reaches a visitor only through arrest or detention; but the practice shows institutions themselves impose the harm, and remedy is unproven.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Conditional: birth-sex custodial placement and isolation documented for a trans detainee, showing how state facilities handle a person whose documents and identity diverge.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Denial upheld by prison administration; no special protection-unit option afforded.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Reaches visitors only if they enter custody; then the institution, not local tolerance, decides placement.

care_services.exposure: Bank service denied to a trans woman over a document/appearance mismatch (2024 review); discrimination reported as commonplace in services.
care_services.protection: Law No. 2 of 2023 bans discrimination on gender identity; Equality Council confirmed the discrimination and recommended preventive measures.
care_services.interaction: Private gatekeepers apply discretion; the equality body names the wrong and recommends, but implementation of the recommendations is unresolved.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Hate speech remains serious with no meaningful national response; election-period political hate speech rose; local and one occupied-region 'propaganda' bans show recurring threat-framing of LGBT expression, though the earlier bans were struck down.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate speech and hate crimes criminalised since 2022 with gender identity and sexual orientation named; courts invalidated local and regional propaganda bans in 2013.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Statute and courts restrain the threat-framing layer, but enforcement and political rhetoric do not; occupied-region enforcement is unsourced.

minors_guardians.interaction: No evidence on how a trans minor or a guardian travelling with one would be treated at borders, in accommodation or in facilities.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Extremely low acceptance (79% would not accept LGBT neighbours; 60% not as colleagues); discrimination and violence described as commonplace; Pride was attacked in 2008 and cancelled after attacks in 2017; no trans-specific violence rate with a denominator is available.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Recent Pride proceeds openly and was police-protected (2018 tear gas against counter-protesters, 2024 march open); hate-crime statute exists.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police protection has improved at the capital's flagship event but was absent elsewhere and earlier, so an outed visitor's ordinary street risk rests on a hostile public with uneven policing.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Access-to-justice barriers identified in a 2024 regional legal analysis; impunity for past violations; equality-body recommendations unenforced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Equality Council confirms discrimination; constitutional court-level review struck down propaganda bans; ombudsman engaged on the prison case.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist and sometimes produce findings, but not outcomes; whether immigration detention, rural policing or occupied-region law would reach a visitor is unanswered.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars trans visitors at the border outright, with routine discretionary refusal and no effective appeal. This dossier documents no entry restriction, no visitor registration and no exclusion practice, so it sits materially above that anchor despite comparable institutional unresponsiveness.

Kestrel Isles documents border officers routing trans travellers to secondary screening and discretionary refusal of admission. Here the record is silent on border treatment and shows no refusal practice, so this jurisdiction is somewhat safer — offset by markedly lower social acceptance and a documented birth-sex custody placement.

Meridia documents trained border officers, entry on markers matching presentation, tribunal appeals and brief, remedied detention. This dossier has thicker anti-discrimination paper but no shown border practice, unenforced recommendations, and documented custodial isolation abuse, placing it clearly below that anchor.

Vesskar exposes every visitor through linked biometric cards and a deceptive-presentation statute with documented detention. This dossier has no such statute or universal verification regime, but pervasive anti-LGBT hostility and unresolved remedies keep it from rising much above that anchor.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is paper-protective and street-hostile. Gender identity is a protected ground, hate crimes are criminalised, courts have struck down local 'propaganda' bans, and recent Pride was policed; the Equality Council even confirmed a service refusal as discrimination. But enforcement is thin — recommendations not implemented, hate speech unanswered, an arson against an LGBT lawyer uninvestigated — and social acceptance is measured as extremely low, so an outed visitor meets refusal, hostility and indifferent policing. Custody is the worst case: a documented trans detainee was placed by birth sex, isolated and humiliated, with the state denying fault. Nothing documents border or facility rules aimed at visitors.
